behavior.arguments: rdi = out pointer (0x34 bytes written); rsi = source record pointer: [rsi+0x00..0x10] and [rsi+0x10..0x20] are the two reversed fields, [rsi+0x20..0x30] the verbatim 16-byte header field, [rsi+0x30..0x34] the verbatim dword. No other argument is read.

edges.first_reversed_field: [rdi+0x14..0x24] = byte-reverse of [rsi+0x10..0x20]; marker edge: out[0x14] == src[0x1f], out[0x23] == src[0x10].
edges.reversal_model: The punpcklbw/hbw + pshufd 0x4e + pshuflw/hw 0x1b + packuswb sequence is an exact 16-byte reversal by word-level construction: widened words are lane-swapped, word-reversed per 64-bit half, and packed back. Verified on bytes 0..15, a marker pattern, and all zeros.
edges.second_reversed_field: [rdi+0x24..0x34] = byte-reverse of [rsi+0x00..0x10]; marker edge: out[0x24] == src[0x0f], out[0x33] == src[0x00].
edges.verbatim_header: [rdi+0x00..0x10] = [rsi+0x20..0x30] verbatim (movups pair); sequential-source edge: out[0x00..0x10] == src[0x20..0x30].

behavior.entry_shape: Opens with mov %rdi,%rax (NOT endbr64); jump-free, zero calls inside, single ret.
behavior.return_rule: Write [rdi+0x00] = [rsi+0x20] (16B verbatim); [rdi+0x10] = dword [rsi+0x30]; [rdi+0x14] = byte-reverse of [rsi+0x10] (16B); [rdi+0x24] = byte-reverse of [rsi] (16B). Total out size 0x34. Return value is the out pointer, incidentally.

coordinate_system: ELF virtual addresses, without a guessed loader or Ghidra rebase. The ELF section table maps .text with file offset = VA - 0x1000; the retained .eh_frame has equal file offset and VA. The tools resolve sections rather than assuming one global VA/file-offset relationship.
